title: Yes, the AI stock selloff looks terrifying. But it might actually save the bull market.
excerpt: The hottest tech trades of 2026 just got slammed — smart investors are buying anyway.
content_html:
Robert Ross

Thu, July 23, 2026 at 6:02 PM EDT 4 min read

After one of the most powerful rallies ever seen, the PHLX Semiconductor Index SOX is now in bear-market territory, dropping more than 20% from its highs. Yet the S&P 500 SPX has withstood the heat and is up almost 10% this year so far.

Investor Michael Burry and other AI bears have spent months warning that the Big Tech capex boom cannot last. To them, this latest selloff will look like vindication. But I see a healthier market emerging from it. The market is rotating, not collapsing.

Most Read from MarketWatch

  • These are the toughest places in America to sell a home right now

  • Lockheed Martin's stock skyrockets as push to build more missiles faster pays off

  • The super rich use 401(k)s and IRAs to sidestep taxes on millions of dollars. This proposed law would cut them off.

Money is not fleeing the market

Look no further than the Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF RSP which hit another all-time high last week. More stocks are also trading above their key 200-day moving averages than at any time this year.

Instead, money is rotating out of the most crowded corners of the market and into sectors including healthcare, financials and select megacap tech companies. That's what expanding breadth looks like, as a bull market supported by several sectors is much sturdier than one balanced on a tower of parabolic semiconductor stocks.

And that's a different story than most of this bull run. AI infrastructure stocks looked like free-money machines. Shares of memory companies such as SanDisk SNDK, server manufacturers including Dell Technologies DELL and chip suppliers like Intel INTC rose so quickly that investors began treating volatility like an extinct species.

That type of market euphoria is never sustainable and is almost always followed by a steep correction.

That's a good thing. A correction releases pressure from the market's most speculative corners. It resets sentiment, lowers valuations and gives earnings time to catch up with prices. And earnings are growing rapidly. Analysts expect semiconductor profits to rise 133% from a year ago and estimate that chip makers alone could account for nearly half of the S&P 500's second-quarter profit growth.

Chip stocks may not have bottomed, but it's close. As I discussed in my latest Substack newsletter, I've been a buyer of AI stocks this week. In my view, the AI investment cycle has not suddenly disappeared just because the stocks stopped going straight up.

But for those who thought the party would never end, you are learning a valuable lesson.

罗伯特·罗斯

2026 年 7 月 23 日星期四，美国东部时间下午 6:02 阅读 4 分钟

在经历了有史以来最强劲的反弹之一后，PHLX 半导体指数 SOX 目前处于熊市区域，较高点​​下跌了 20% 以上。 然而，标准普尔 500 SPX 指数经受住了考验，今年迄今已上涨近 10%。

投资者迈克尔·伯里（Michael Burry）和其他人工智能看空者花了几个月的时间警告说，大型科技资本支出的繁荣不会持续下去。 对他们来说，最近的抛售看起来像是一种平反。 但我看到一个更健康的市场正在崛起。 市场正在旋转，而不是崩溃。

大多数阅读来自 MarketWatch

  • 这些是美国目前最难卖房的地方
  • 随着更快地制造更多导弹的努力取得回报，洛克希德·马丁公司的股价飙升
  • 超级富豪使用 401(k) 和 IRA 来逃避数百万美元的税收。 这项拟议的法律将切断他们的联系。
资金并未逃离市场

Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF RSP 就是最好的例子，该指数上周再创历史新高。 交易价格高于关键 200 日移动平均线的股票数量也比今年任何时候都多。

相反，资金正从市场最拥挤的角落转向医疗保健、金融和精选的大型科技公司等领域。 这就是扩大广度的样子，因为由多个板块支撑的牛市比抛物线半导体股票塔平衡的牛市要坚固得多。

这与本次牛市的大部分情况不同。 人工智能基础设施股票看起来就像免费赚钱机器。 SanDisk SNDK等内存公司、Dell Technologies DELL等服务器制造商以及Intel INTC等芯片供应商的股价上涨如此之快，以至于投资者开始将波动性视为灭绝物种。

这种类型的市场兴奋永远不会持续，并且几乎总是伴随着急剧的调整。

这是一件好事。 调整释放了市场最具投机性的压力。 它重置了市场情绪，降低了估值，并为盈利提供了追赶价格的时间。 而且收入正在快速增长。 分析师预计半导体利润将比一年前增长 133%，并估计仅芯片制造商就可以贡献标准普尔 500 指数第二季度利润增长的近一半。

芯片股可能尚未触底，但已接近触底。 正如我在最新的 Substack 时事通讯中讨论的那样，我本周一直在购买人工智能股票。 在我看来，人工智能投资周期并没有因为股票停止直线上涨而突然消失。

但对于那些认为聚会永远不会结束的人来说，你正在学到宝贵的一课。
